name: Summer landscape-painting school at the old station (UW Department of Painting, Sculpture and Design)
description: When the biological station moved to Point Caution, UW art professor John Butler ran a six-week landscape painting and drawing course (June 16 to July 25, 1924) in the old station quarters in Friday Harbor. Seattle donors gave scholarships, and the press called it the start of an artists' colony. No source found shows it running again after 1924.

name: Helen Riaboff Whiteley Center (scholars, writers and artists of any field)
description: Retreat of studies and cottages on the FHL campus built by UW biologist Arthur Whiteley in memory of Helen Riaboff Whiteley, open to scholars from every discipline, including poets, writers, composers, photographers and visual artists. It hosted 100-200+ scholars a year, published sample scholar lists in the annual newsletter, and from 2022 has offered need-based Whiteley Fellowships (Arthur & Helen Whiteley Distinguished Fellow Endowment).

name: Macfarlane Art Studio (studio for visual artists attached to the Whiteley Center)
description: A former caretaker's garage on the main campus road, converted with money from Advancement Board members Robert (Robbie) and Jan Macfarlane into a skylit studio for visiting artists. Arthur Whiteley and director Dennis Willows oversaw the conversion over about ten years. It was in use by artists from at least 2005, got new glass doors by 2017, and is supported by a Macfarlane Art Studio Endowment.

name: FHL Artist in Residence Fellowship (Macfarlane Art Studio Fellowship / Macfarlane Artist Fellowship)
description: Donor-funded fellowship giving visual artists housing, honoraria and exclusive use of the Macfarlane Art Studio. In 2018-2021 it covered stays of up to a month. From about 2023 it was renamed the Artist in Residence Program: several fellowships a year, October to May, for 1-3 months, for projects tied to marine science or the environment, with fellows giving back through lessons, talks or art FHL can use.

name: Friday Harbor Photography Workshop at the Whiteley Center
description: A week-long art photography workshop in traditional black-and-white photography (field, darkroom and studio) for about six participants chosen by national juried competition. Rod Dresser led it, with Huntington Witherill in 2006. The Macfarlanes and Freestyle Photographic sponsored it.

name: Poetry and creative writing at FHL (UW English): poetry classes, autumn literature-and-marine-biology quarter, Poetry and Science Symposium
years: c. 2005-present (poetry class from c. 2005; earlier symposium version mid-to-late 2000s; autumn quarter from 2012; annual symposium from c. 2012, still held in 2023)
description: UW poets ran an early-fall poetry class at the labs for about seven years before 2012, and an earlier version of the Poetry and Science Symposium ran in the mid-to-late 2000s. Richard Kenney then built an autumn quarter in which English courses (ENGL 365 Reading and Writing the Marine Environment, ENGL 493 workshop) run alongside marine biology. Out of this came the annual Poetry and Science Symposium each November (from c. 2012), pairing poets and scientists such as Adam Summers. In 2026 Summers was awarded the 2025-26 Rome Prize in Environmental Arts & Humanities for "Piscis Romana", in partnership with Katharine Ogle, lecturer in English at the University of Southern California.

name: Marine Sciences, Ocean Arts: Interdisciplinary, Intertidal, Interdependent (training workshop)
description: A three-week summer workshop for scientists, artists, educators and students in marine STEAM, combining field and lab science with ecopoetics, bioart and other arts. Endorsed by the UN Ocean Decade and taught by Marjorie Wonham, Xochitl Clare and Genevieve Gaiser Tremblay, with guest speakers (Drew Harvell, Melody Jue, Sierra Nelson, Rena Priest, Josie Iselin, Samantha-Lynn Martinez, Amelia Nommensen, Adam Summers, Lekelia Jenkins, Astrida Neimanis, Fernanda Oyarzun). Participants made works in poetry, photography, ceramics, cyanotype, anthotype, watercolor, weaving, collage and installation, including costumes from beach plastics.

name: Jazz at the Labs (annual concert fundraiser)
description: A yearly dinner and jazz concert at FHL, set up by development officer Bob Schwartzberg, raising money for the FHL K-12 Science Outreach Program. Performers included saxophonist Ron Howell (Jazz Oracle, Chimera), director Dennis Willows with the San Juan Jazz Quartet/Quintet, and Chris Amemiya (a scientist and Whiteley Scholar) with Jazz Coalescence. This is a performance series, not a residency, so its musicians are not listed as artists.

name: Art installed or restored on the FHL campus
description: Permanent works on campus: Julian Voss-Andreae's stainless-steel "Steel Jellyfish" (2006), located at FHL, where GFP was discovered; a 1927 Nuu-chah-nulth totem pole carved by Wilson A. Williams, donated by Eugene Nester (a Whiteley committee member) and restored at FHL in spring 2023 by carvers Rick Williams and EagleSon Williams; and a carved stone bench by local artist Tom Small honoring Joann Otto (2025). The Whiteley Center also keeps an art collection documented in a photo book.

name: Art-science work from the Summers lab (photography, SEM imaging, poetry pairings, artist training)
description: FHL biologist Adam Summers exhibited his cleared-and-stained fish photographs as art, paired with poems by Sierra Nelson. He taught photographer Robert Dash to use the lab's scanning electron microscope (c. 2014), helped bring artist Fernanda Oyarzun back to FHL in 2023, and in 2024 and 2025 held Maxwell Hanrahan Foundation grants to support an artist/illustrator in training. In 2026 he was awarded the 2025-26 Rome Prize in Environmental Arts & Humanities for "Piscis Romana", in partnership with Katharine Ogle (USC). Summers is an FHL scientist, so this is a collaboration based in a lab rather than a residency.
